result.label: Tax saved by the child tax credit

status.none: No child qualifies this year. Check the year table below to see when the credit starts.
status.noTax: Your tax is already 0 KRW, so the credit has nothing to reduce.
status.partial: Your tax is only {tax} KRW, so it falls by that much. Unused child credit is not carried forward — if you both work, try moving children to your spouse below.
status.full: The {credit} KRW credit plus 10% local income tax comes straight off your tax.

credits.rule: 250,000 KRW for one child, 550,000 KRW for two, plus 400,000 KRW for each child from the third. Birth/adoption: 300,000 KRW for a first child, 500,000 KRW for a second, 700,000 KRW for a third or later (Income Tax Act Art. 59-2).

reason.ok: Age {age} — eligible for tax year {year} (born in {bornBy} or earlier).
reason.young: Age {age} — for tax year {year} only children born in {bornBy} or earlier qualify. The eligible age went up as the child allowance was extended to older children. Eligible from tax year {from}.
reason.y2017: Born in {excluded} — eligible for tax year 2025, but the 2026 amendment's transitional rule excludes tax years 2026–2029 (child allowance extension). Eligible again from tax year {from} (age 13).
reason.newborn: Born this year — the child tax credit starts in tax year {from}. This year you get the birth/adoption credit instead.
reason.over: Age {age} — over 20, so not a basic dependent and not eligible for the credit. There is no age limit for a child with a disability.

span.range: Eligible for tax years {from}–{to} ({n} years, until age 20)
span.open: Eligible from tax year {from} onward (no dependent age limit with a disability)

relNote.grandchild: A grandchild cannot be claimed if a parent or another relative already claims them as a dependent. Grandchildren do not get the birth/adoption credit.
relNote.foster: A foster child must meet the conditions set by the enforcement decree (such as how long you raised them) for the dependent deduction and the credit.

childTaxCredit.basicNote: Separately from this credit, each of the {n} dependent children gives a 1.5M KRW income deduction ({amount} KRW in total). That is not included above.

share.headlineZero: No child tax credit this year
share.text: With gross pay of {salaryM}M KRW, {eligible} of {n} children qualify for the child tax credit this year — a {credit} KRW credit and {saving} KRW less tax.

actions.full: Open in the year-end tax calculator
actions.fullNote: Opens with your number of children, excluded children and birth order filled in. Add cards, pensions and medical costs to see your total refund.

couple.title: Dual income: who should claim the children?
couple.desc: Each child is claimed by only one spouse, and the 1.5M KRW dependent deduction goes with the child tax credit. Every split is compared to find the lowest combined tax.
couple.hint: Enter it if you both work. Leave it blank for a single income.
couple.empty: Enter your spouse's gross pay to compare who should claim the children.
couple.noKids: There are no dependent children to split.
couple.keep: Keeping all children on your return is best. Moving them all to your spouse would raise your combined tax by {diff} KRW.
couple.same: Your combined tax is the same whoever claims the children.
couple.moveAll: Moving all children to your spouse lowers your combined tax by {gain} KRW.
couple.split: Splitting the children as below lowers your combined tax by {gain} KRW compared with claiming them all yourself.
couple.caption: Combined tax by split (including local income tax)
couple.note: Tax is the annual determined tax including local income tax. This is an estimate that assumes no deductions other than salary for each of you, and puts the birth/adoption credit with whoever claims the youngest child. To split parents and other relatives too, use the dependent deduction checker.

years.title: Year table by child
years.desc: Filled cells are the tax years in which the child tax credit applies. For tax years 2026–2029 the transitional rule raises the eligible age by one each year, and from tax year 2030 it is 13 or older. It ends after age 20 (except for a disability).

rules.title: Eligible age by tax year
rules.note: An age counts if it applies on any day of the year (Income Tax Act Art. 53(5)), so it is judged by birth year. Tax year 2025 used the old rule of 8 or older; from tax year 2026 this follows the Income Tax Act as amended on April 21, 2026 and Article 2 of its addenda.

tips.title: Good to know
items: The child tax credit is applied when you register the child as a dependent in your employer's year-end settlement. No extra documents are needed.
A child born this year is too young for the child tax credit, but you get the birth/adoption credit. It is claimed once, in that year only.
Children born in 2017 were eligible for tax year 2025 but are excluded for 2026–2029. They become eligible again from tax year 2030 (settled in early 2031).
With two incomes the higher earner usually benefits more, but if one spouse has little tax, splitting can be better. Check the comparison above.
If a child has income such as a part-time job (income over 1M KRW a year, or gross pay over 5M KRW if it is only wages), they are no longer a dependent and the credit is lost too.
From the year a child turns 21, both the dependent deduction and the child tax credit end. A child with a disability stays eligible at any age.
